title.zh: 卷五十六 志第四十六 刑法
title.raw: 卷五十六 志第四十六 刑法 Volume 56 Treatises 52: Punishment and Law

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 25%古之為國者，議事以制，不為刑辟，懼民之知爭端也。

translations.literal: In antiquity those who governed states deliberated on affairs to establish regulation, and did not create penal statutes, fearing that the people would learn the points of contention.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times, rulers governed by deliberating on affairs to set policy, not by drafting penal codes—they feared teaching the people where disputes might arise.

sentences.zh: 後世作為刑書，惟恐不備，俾民之知所避也。

translations.literal: Later ages composed penal books, fearing only that they might be incomplete, so as to enable the people to know what to avoid.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations wrote penal statutes and worried only that they might be incomplete, so that the people would know what to shun.

sentences.zh: 其為法雖殊，而用心則一，蓋皆欲民之無犯也。

translations.literal: Although their methods of law differed, their intent was one: all wished that the people would not offend.
translations.idiomatic: Though their legal methods differed, their aim was the same: to keep the people from breaking the law.

sentences.zh: 然未知夫導之以德、齊之以禮，而可使民遷善遠罪而不自知也。

translations.literal: Yet they did not know that guiding them with virtue and regulating them with ritual could cause the people to turn toward goodness and keep away from crime without their knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: They did not yet understand that guiding the people with virtue and harmonizing them through ritual could move them toward goodness and away from crime almost without their noticing.

sentences.zh: 唐之刑書有四，曰：律、令、格、式。

translations.literal: The Tang penal books were four in number, called: the Code, Ordinances, Administrative Rules, and Formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Tang criminal law comprised four kinds of writings: the Code, Ordinances, Administrative Rules, and Formulas.

sentences.zh: 令者，尊卑貴賤之等數，國家之制度也；

translations.literal: Ordinances were the gradations of noble and base, exalted and humble, and the institutions of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinances defined ranks from high to low and the institutions of the realm.

sentences.zh: 格者，百官有司之所常行之事也；

translations.literal: Administrative Rules were the matters that the hundred officials and their departments regularly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Administrative Rules recorded what the various offices routinely did in practice.

sentences.zh: 式者，其所常守之法也。

translations.literal: Formulas were the laws they regularly observed.
translations.idiomatic: Formulas were the standard procedures they were to follow.

sentences.zh: 凡邦國之政，必從事於此三者。

translations.literal: In all governance of the realm, one had to attend to these three.
translations.idiomatic: All affairs of state had to proceed according to these three.

sentences.zh: 其有所違及人之為惡而入于罪戾者，一斷以律。

translations.literal: Where there were violations, and where people did evil and entered into guilt, all were adjudicated solely by the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Any breach of them, or any evil act that brought a person within the scope of punishment, was decided solely under the Code.

sentences.zh: 律之為書，因隋之舊，為十有二篇：一曰名例，二曰衞禁，三曰職制，四曰戶婚，五曰廄庫，六曰擅興，七曰賊盜，八曰鬬訟，九曰詐偽，十曰雜律，十一曰捕亡，十二曰斷獄。

translations.literal: The Code as a book followed the Sui precedent and had twelve sections: first, General Provisions; second, Imperial Guard and Prohibitions; third, Official Regulations; fourth, Household and Marriage; fifth, Stables and Storehouses; sixth, Unauthorized Mobilization; seventh, Banditry and Theft; eighth, Assault and Litigation; ninth, Fraud and Forgery; tenth, Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh, Apprehension of Fugitives; twelfth, Trial and Punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The Code followed the Sui model in twelve chapters: General Provisions; Imperial Guard and Prohibitions; Official Regulations; Household and Marriage; Stables and Storehouses; Unauthorized Mobilization; Banditry and Theft; Assault and Litigation; Fraud and Forgery; Miscellaneous Statutes; Apprehension of Fugitives; and Trial and Punishment.

sentences.zh: 其用刑有五：一曰笞。

translations.literal: The application of punishment had five kinds: first, beating with the light stick.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments were of five kinds. The first was beating with the light stick.

sentences.zh: 笞之為言恥也；

translations.literal: The word for chi means shame.
translations.idiomatic: The term chi means shame.

sentences.zh: 凡過之小者，捶撻以恥之。

translations.literal: For all minor offenses, one flogged and beat to shame them.
translations.idiomatic: Minor offenses were punished by flogging meant to humiliate.

sentences.zh: 漢用竹，後世更以楚。

translations.literal: The Han used bamboo; later ages changed to use the chu stick.
translations.idiomatic: The Han used bamboo rods; later dynasties switched to the chu stick.

sentences.zh: 書曰「扑作教刑」是也。

translations.literal: The Book says, "Beating serves as corrective punishment"—this is that.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Classic means by "beating as corrective punishment."

sentences.zh: 二曰杖。

translations.literal: Second was beating with the heavy stick.
translations.idiomatic: Second was beating with the heavy stick.

sentences.zh: 杖者，持也：可持以擊也。

translations.literal: Zhang means to hold: one could hold it to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang means "to hold"—a staff one could grasp to strike with.

sentences.zh: 書曰「鞭作官刑」是也。

translations.literal: The Book says, "The whip serves as official punishment"—this is that.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the Classic means by "the whip as official punishment."

sentences.zh: 三曰徒。

translations.literal: Third was penal servitude.
translations.idiomatic: Third was penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 徒者，奴也；

translations.literal: Tu means slave.
translations.idiomatic: Tu means slave.

sentences.zh: 蓋奴辱之。

translations.literal: It was essentially to enslave and humiliate them.
translations.idiomatic: It reduced the offender to servile humiliation.

sentences.zh: 周禮曰：其奴，男子入于罪隸，任之以事，寘之圜土而教之，量其罪之輕重，有年數而捨。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou say: as slaves, the men entered criminal servitude, were assigned tasks, placed in the walled compound and instructed, and according to the lightness or heaviness of the crime, after a set number of years they were released.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou state that male offenders became criminal bondsmen, were put to labor, confined within the round compound for instruction, and released after a term measured to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 四曰流。

translations.literal: Fourth was exile.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth was exile.

sentences.zh: 書云「流宥五刑」，謂不忍刑殺，宥之于遠也。

translations.literal: The Book says, "Exile pardons the five punishments," meaning that one could not bear to punish by killing and pardoned them in the distance.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says, "Exile commutes the five punishments"—because the court could not bear to execute the offender and instead spared him by banishment to a distant place.

sentences.zh: 五曰死。

translations.literal: Fifth was death.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth was death.

sentences.zh: 乃古大辟之刑也。

translations.literal: This was the ancient punishment of the great execution.
translations.idiomatic: This was the ancient supreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 自隋以前，死刑有五，曰：罄、絞、斬、梟、裂。

translations.literal: Before the Sui, capital punishment had five kinds, called: strangulation by bowstring, strangulation by cord, decapitation, exposure of the head, and dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Before the Sui, there were five forms of capital punishment: strangulation with a bowstring, strangulation with a cord, decapitation, exposure of the severed head, and dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 而流、徒之刑，鞭笞兼用，數皆踰百。

translations.literal: As for exile and penal servitude, whip and light-stick beatings were used together, and the counts all exceeded one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and penal servitude were often combined with flogging and beating, sometimes totaling more than a hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 至隋始定為：笞刑五，自十至于五十；

translations.literal: By the Sui it was first fixed as: five grades of chi punishment, from ten to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui first standardized five grades of chi, from ten to fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 杖刑五，自六十至于百；

translations.literal: Five grades of zhang punishment, from sixty to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Five grades of zhang, from sixty to one hundred;

sentences.zh: 徒刑五，自一年至于三年；

translations.literal: Five grades of tu punishment, from one year to three years.
translations.idiomatic: five grades of penal servitude, from one to three years;

sentences.zh: 流刑三，自一千里至于二千里；

translations.literal: Three grades of exile, from one thousand li to two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: three grades of exile, from one thousand to two thousand li;

sentences.zh: 死刑二，絞、斬。

translations.literal: Two kinds of capital punishment: strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: and two forms of capital punishment: strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 除其鞭刑及梟首、轘裂之酷。

translations.literal: They abolished the whip punishment and the cruel punishments of exposing the head and cart-splitting.
translations.idiomatic: They abolished flogging as well as the cruel penalties of exposing the head and tearing the body apart with carts.

sentences.zh: 又有議、請、減、贖、當、免之法。

translations.literal: There were also the methods of deliberation, petition, reduction, commutation by payment, offset, and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: There were also provisions for deliberation, petition, reduction, ransom, offset, and exemption from punishment.

sentences.zh: 唐皆因之。

translations.literal: The Tang all followed these.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang adopted all of these.

sentences.zh: 然隋文帝性刻深，而煬帝昏亂，民不勝其毒。

translations.literal: Yet Emperor Wen of Sui was by nature harsh and deep, and Emperor Yang was muddled and disorderly, and the people could not bear their poison.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Emperor Wen of Sui was harsh by nature, and Emperor Yang was corrupt and chaotic, so the people could not endure their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 唐興，高祖入京師，約法十二條，惟殺人、劫盜、背軍、叛逆者死。

translations.literal: When the Tang arose, Gaozu entered the capital and made a compact law of twelve articles; only for murder, robbery, desertion, and rebellion was death imposed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tang rose, Gaozu entered the capital and proclaimed a twelve-article compact: only murder, robbery, desertion, and treason were capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，命納言劉文靜等損益律令。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, he ordered the Palace Counselor Liu Wenjing and others to revise the code and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: After he accepted the abdication, he ordered Palace Counselor Liu Wenjing and others to revise the code and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，頒新格五十三條，唯吏受賕、犯盜、詐冒府庫物，赦不原。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, fifty-three new administrative rules were promulgated; only for officials receiving bribes, committing theft, and fraudulently taking goods from government storehouses was amnesty not granted.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2, fifty-three new administrative rules were issued; only bribery by officials, theft, and fraud involving government storehouses were excluded from amnesty.

sentences.zh: 凡斷屠日及正月、五月、九月不行刑。

translations.literal: On all days when slaughter was forbidden, and in the first, fifth, and ninth months, punishments were not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were suspended on meat-abstention days and in the first, fifth, and ninth months.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖躬錄囚徒，以人因亂冒法者眾，盜非劫傷其主及征人逃亡、官吏枉法，皆原之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners; because many people in the chaos had violated the law, for theft that was not robbery injuring the owner, and for conscripts who fled and officials who perverted the law, all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Gaozu personally reviewed prisoners. Because many had broken the law amid the turmoil, he pardoned all except robbers who injured their victims, deserters from military service, and officials who had perverted justice.

sentences.zh: 已而又詔僕射裴寂等十五人更撰律令，凡律五百，麗以五十三條。

translations.literal: Afterward he again ordered the Vice Director Pei Ji and fifteen others to compile the code and ordinances anew; the code in all had five hundred articles, supplemented by fifty-three articles.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Vice Director Pei Ji and fourteen others to draft a new code and ordinances: five hundred articles of code, supplemented by fifty-three additional provisions.

sentences.zh: 流罪三，皆加千里；

translations.literal: The three grades of exile were all increased by one thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: All three grades of exile were increased by one thousand li.

sentences.zh: 居作三歲至二歲半者悉為一歲。

translations.literal: Terms of labor service from three years down to two and a half years were all made one year.
translations.idiomatic: Terms of compulsory labor from three years down to two and a half were all reduced to one year.

sentences.zh: 餘無改焉。

translations.literal: The rest was unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise nothing was changed.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，詔長孫无忌、房玄齡等復定舊令，議絞刑之屬五十，皆免死而斷右趾。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to revise the old ordinances again; fifty offenses in the category of strangulation were all exempted from death and punished by cutting off the right foot instead.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong ascended the throne, he ordered Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, and others to revise the old ordinances. Fifty offenses punishable by strangulation were commuted from death to amputation of the right foot.

sentences.zh: 既而又哀其斷毀支體，謂侍臣曰：「肉刑，前代除之久矣，今復斷人趾，吾不忍也。

translations.literal: Afterward he again pitied that their limbs were cut and destroyed, and said to his attendant ministers: "Corporal punishments were abolished by former ages long ago; now to cut off people's toes again—I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: But he soon took pity on mutilating the body and told his ministers, "Corporal punishments were abolished long ago. To cut off a man's toes again—I cannot bear it.

sentences.zh: 」王珪、蕭瑀、陳叔達對曰：「受刑者當死而獲生，豈憚去一趾？

translations.literal: Wang Gui, Xiao Yu, and Chen Shuda replied: "Those who receive punishment ought to die yet obtain life—how would they fear losing one toe?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, Xiao Yu, and Chen Shuda replied, "A man who deserves death but is allowed to live—would he shrink from losing a toe?

sentences.zh: 去趾，所以使見者知懼。

translations.literal: Removing the toe is to make those who see know fear.
translations.idiomatic: Amputation warns others and inspires fear.

sentences.zh: 今以死刑為斷趾，蓋寬之也。

translations.literal: Now to substitute cutting off the toe for the death penalty is essentially to leniently treat them.
translations.idiomatic: Replacing execution with toe amputation is itself an act of mercy.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公等更思之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You gentlemen think on it again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Think on it again.

sentences.zh: 」其後蜀王法曹參軍裴弘獻駮律令四十餘事，乃詔房玄齡與弘獻等重加刪定。

translations.literal: Afterward the legal bureau aide of the Prince of Shu, Pei Hongxian, submitted more than forty items criticizing the code and ordinances, and thereupon an edict ordered Fang Xuanling together with Hongxian and others to revise and fix them again.
translations.idiomatic: Later Pei Hongxian, a legal aide under the Prince of Shu, submitted more than forty criticisms of the code and ordinances, and the emperor ordered Fang Xuanling and Hongxian to revise them again.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等以謂「古者五刑，刖居其一。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others said: "In antiquity the five punishments included amputation as one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and the others argued, "In antiquity the five punishments included mutilation.

sentences.zh: 及肉刑既廢，今以笞、杖、徒、流、死為五刑，而又刖足，是六刑也」。

translations.literal: When corporal punishments had already been abolished, now to take chi, zhang, tu, exile, and death as the five punishments, and again to amputate the foot—this would be six punishments."
translations.idiomatic: Corporal punishments were abolished long ago; if chi, zhang, penal servitude, exile, and death are the five punishments, adding foot amputation would make six."

sentences.zh: 於是除斷趾法，為加役流三千里，居作二年。

translations.literal: Thereupon they abolished the law of cutting off the toe and made it penal servitude with added labor at three thousand li, with two years of labor service.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore abolished toe amputation and substituted exile to three thousand li with two years of penal labor.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗覽明堂針灸圖，見人之五藏皆近背，針灸失所，則其害致死，歎曰：「夫箠者，五刑之輕；

translations.literal: Taizong once perused the Hall of Enlightenment acupuncture chart and saw that the five viscera of the human body all lay near the back; if acupuncture missed its place, the harm could cause death. He sighed and said: "Beating is the lightest of the five punishments;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once studied an acupuncture chart of the Hall of Enlightenment and saw that the vital organs lie close to the back; a misplaced needle could kill. He sighed and said, "Flogging is the lightest of the five punishments,

sentences.zh: 死者，人之所重。

translations.literal: death is what people regard as weighty.
translations.idiomatic: yet death is what people value most.

sentences.zh: 安得犯至輕之刑而或致死？

translations.literal: How can one commit the lightest punishment and yet sometimes die?
translations.idiomatic: How can the lightest punishment sometimes bring death?

sentences.zh: 」遂詔罪人無得鞭背。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered that criminals must not be flogged on the back.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore decreed that criminals must not be flogged on the back.

sentences.zh: 五年，河內人李好德坐妖言下獄，大理丞張蘊古以為好德病狂瞀，法不當坐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Li Haode of Henei was imprisoned for heterodox speech; the Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Zhang Yungu held that Haode was ill with mad delusion and by law should not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Li Haode of Henei was imprisoned for seditious talk. Assistant Director Zhang Yungu of the Court of Judicial Review argued that Haode was insane and not liable under the law.

sentences.zh: 治書侍御史權萬紀劾蘊古相州人，好德兄厚德方為相州刺史，故蘊古奏不以實。

translations.literal: The Investigating Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, saying he was a man of Xiangzhou; Haode's elder brother Houde was then prefect of Xiangzhou, and therefore Yungu's memorial was not according to fact.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Quan Wanji impeached Yungu, noting that Yungu was from Xiangzhou while Haode's elder brother Houde was then prefect there, and alleging that Yungu had falsified his report.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒，遽斬蘊古，既而大悔，因詔「死刑雖令即決，皆三覆奏」。

translations.literal: Taizong was angry and immediately executed Yungu; afterward he greatly regretted it and therefore issued an edict: "Although capital punishment may be ordered for immediate decision, in all cases there shall be threefold re-submission."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong in anger had Yungu executed at once, then deeply regretted it and decreed that even when capital punishment was ordered for immediate execution, it must be submitted for review three times.

sentences.zh: 久之，謂羣臣曰：「死者不可復生。

translations.literal: After a long time he said to the assembled ministers: "The dead cannot live again.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he told his ministers, "The dead cannot be brought back to life.

sentences.zh: 昔王世充殺鄭頲而猶能悔，近有府史取賕不多，朕殺之，是思之不審也。

translations.literal: In the past Wang Shichong killed Zheng Ting and still could repent; recently there was a prefectural clerk who took not much in bribes, and I killed him—this was failure to deliberate carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong killed Zheng Ting and still repented; recently I executed a prefectural clerk who had taken only a small bribe—that was careless thinking.

sentences.zh: 決囚雖三覆奏，而頃刻之間，何暇思慮？

translations.literal: Although deciding prisoners had threefold re-submission, in the space of a moment, what leisure was there for reflection?
translations.idiomatic: Even with threefold review, what time is there to reflect in a few moments?

sentences.zh: 自今宜二日五覆奏。

translations.literal: From now on there should be fivefold re-submission over two days.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth there shall be five reviews over two days.

sentences.zh: 決日，尚食勿進酒肉，教坊太常輟教習，諸州死罪三覆奏，其日亦蔬食，務合禮撤樂、減膳之意。

translations.literal: On the day of decision, the Imperial Kitchen was not to serve wine or meat; the Music Office and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were to cease instruction and practice; in all prefectures for capital crimes there was threefold re-submission, and on that day they also ate vegetarian food, striving to accord with the ritual meaning of withdrawing music and reducing meals.
translations.idiomatic: On execution day the Imperial Kitchen was to serve no meat or wine, the Music Office and Court of Imperial Sacrifices were to suspend performances, and provinces reviewing capital cases were likewise to abstain from meat—observing the ritual spirit of withdrawing music and reducing the imperial table.

sentences.zh: 故時律，兄弟分居，蔭不相及，而連坐則俱死。

translations.literal: Under the law of that time, when brothers lived separately their inherited privilege did not extend to one another, yet for collective punishment all were put to death together.
translations.idiomatic: Under the earlier code, brothers who lived apart did not share inherited privilege, yet collective punishment still meant death for all.

sentences.zh: 同州人房彊以弟謀反當從坐，帝因錄囚為之動容，曰：「反逆有二：興師動眾一也，惡言犯法二也。

translations.literal: Fang Qiang of Tongzhou, because his younger brother plotted rebellion, was to suffer collective punishment; the emperor, while reviewing prisoners, was moved for his sake and said: "Rebellion has two kinds: raising troops is one; evil speech violating the law is two.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qiang of Tongzhou was to be punished because his brother had plotted rebellion. While reviewing prisoners the emperor was moved and said, "Treason takes two forms: raising an army, and seditious words that violate the law.

sentences.zh: 輕重固異，而鈞謂之反，連坐皆死，豈定法耶？

translations.literal: Light and heavy are certainly different, yet equally they are called rebellion, and collective punishment puts all to death—is this settled law?
translations.idiomatic: Their gravity differs, yet both are called treason and kin are executed together—is that settled law?

sentences.zh: 」玄齡等議曰：「禮，孫為父尸，故祖有蔭孫令，是祖孫重而兄弟輕。

translations.literal: Xuanling and others deliberated and said: "According to ritual, the grandson stands in the place of the father, and therefore the ordinance grants the grandfather privilege extending to the grandson—thus grandfather and grandson are weighty while brothers are light.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others argued, "By ritual the grandson represents the father, so privilege extends from grandfather to grandson—grandfather and grandson weigh more heavily than brothers.

sentences.zh: 」於是令：反逆者，祖孫與兄弟緣坐，皆配沒；

translations.literal: Thereupon the ordinance provided: for rebellion, grandfather, grandson, and brothers who suffered collective punishment were all sentenced to confiscation and exile.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore ordained that in cases of armed rebellion, grandparents, grandchildren, and brothers implicated by kinship were all sentenced to confiscation and exile;

sentences.zh: 惡言犯法者，兄弟配流而已。

translations.literal: For evil speech violating the law, brothers were sentenced only to exile.
translations.idiomatic: for seditious speech alone, brothers were exiled and no more.

sentences.zh: 玄齡等遂與法司增損隋律，降大辟為流者九十二，流為徒者七十一，以為律；

translations.literal: Xuanling and others then together with the legal offices revised the Sui code, reducing great execution to exile in ninety-two cases and exile to penal servitude in seventy-one cases, and made this the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and the legal offices then revised the Sui code, commuting capital punishment to exile in ninety-two articles and exile to penal servitude in seventy-one, producing the Code.

sentences.zh: 定令一千五百四十六條，以為令；

translations.literal: They fixed one thousand five hundred forty-six articles as Ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: They compiled 1,546 articles as Ordinances;

sentences.zh: 又刪武德以來敕三千餘條為七百條，以為格；

translations.literal: They also culled more than three thousand edicts since Wude down to seven hundred articles as Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: They pared more than three thousand edicts since Wude to seven hundred Administrative Rules;

sentences.zh: 又取尚書省列曹及諸寺、監、十六衞計帳以為式。

translations.literal: They also took the account ledgers of the various bureaus of the Secretariat and the various directorates, offices, and Sixteen Guards as Formulas.
translations.idiomatic: and drew on the account ledgers of the Secretariat bureaus, directorates, offices, and Sixteen Guards for the Formulas.

sentences.zh: 凡州縣皆有獄，而京兆、河南獄治京師，其諸司有罪及金吾捕者又有大理獄。

translations.literal: All prefectures and counties had prisons; the prisons of Jingzhao and Henan administered the capital; for offenses by the various offices and those arrested by the Gold Crow Guard there was also the Court of Judicial Review prison.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and county had a prison; Jingzhao and Henan administered prisons for the capital; officials of the central offices and persons arrested by the Gold Crow Guard were held in the Court of Judicial Review prison.

sentences.zh: 京師之囚，刑部月一奏，御史巡行之。

translations.literal: Prisoners in the capital were reported monthly by the Ministry of Justice, and censors made inspection rounds.
translations.idiomatic: Capital prisoners were reported monthly to the Ministry of Justice, and censors conducted inspections.

sentences.zh: 每歲立春至秋及大祭祀、致齊，朔望、上下弦、二十四氣、雨及夜未明，假日、斷屠月，皆停死刑。

translations.literal: Each year from the Beginning of Spring to autumn, and on great sacrifices and days of ritual purification, on new and full moon, upper and lower quarter moon, the twenty-four solar terms, rainy days and before dawn, holidays, and months when slaughter was forbidden—all capital punishment was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Each year from Beginning of Spring through autumn, and on major sacrifices, purification days, new and full moons, quarter moons, the twenty-four solar terms, rainy days, before dawn, holidays, and meat-abstention months, capital punishment was suspended.

sentences.zh: 京師決死，涖以御史、金吾，在外則上佐，餘皆判官涖之。

translations.literal: For capital executions in the capital, censors and Gold Crow Guards supervised; outside the capital the chief aide supervised; all others were supervised by judicial officers.
translations.idiomatic: Capital executions in the capital were supervised by censors and Gold Crow Guards; in the provinces by the chief aide; elsewhere by judicial officers.

sentences.zh: 五品以上罪論死，乘車就刑，大理正涖之，或賜死于家。

translations.literal: For officials of fifth rank and above sentenced to death, they rode in a carriage to the place of execution, supervised by the Director of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of fifth rank and above rode to the place of execution under supervision of the Court of Judicial Review, or were granted death at home.

sentences.zh: 凡囚已刑，無親屬者，將作給棺，瘞于京城七里外，壙有甎銘，上揭以榜，家人得取以葬。

translations.literal: For all prisoners already punished who had no kin, the Directorate of Palace Buildings provided coffins; they were buried seven li outside the capital wall; the tomb had brick inscriptions and a placard posted above, so that family members could take them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Executed prisoners without kin received coffins from the Directorate of Palace Buildings and were buried seven li outside the capital, with brick inscriptions and posted notices so relatives could claim the remains.

sentences.zh: 諸獄之長官，五日一慮囚。

translations.literal: The chiefs of all prisons reviewed prisoners once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Prison wardens reviewed cases every five days.

sentences.zh: 夏置漿飲，月一沐之；

translations.literal: In summer they provided broth and drink, and bathed them once a month.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they were given broth and bathed once a month;

sentences.zh: 疾病給醫藥，重者釋械，其家一人入侍，職事散官三品以上，婦女子孫二人入侍。

translations.literal: When ill they were given medicine; the seriously ill were released from fetters; one person from the family entered to attend; for officials of third rank and above in regular or honorary office, two women, children, or grandchildren entered to attend.
translations.idiomatic: the sick received medicine, the seriously ill were unfettered, and one family member could attend; for officials of third rank and above, two wives, children, or grandchildren could attend.

sentences.zh: 天下疑獄讞大理寺不能決，尚書省眾議之，錄可為法者送祕書省。

translations.literal: Doubtful cases throughout the realm that the Court of Judicial Review could not decide were deliberated collectively by the Secretariat; those that could serve as precedents were recorded and sent to the Secretariat Archive.
translations.idiomatic: Cases the Court of Judicial Review could not decide were debated by the Secretariat, and precedents worthy of becoming law were sent to the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 奏報不馳驛。

translations.literal: Memorial reports were not sent by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: Reports were not sent by express relay.

sentences.zh: 經覆而決者，刑部歲以正月遣使巡覆，所至，閱獄囚杻校、糧餉，治不如法者。

translations.literal: For those decided after review, the Ministry of Justice each year in the first month dispatched envoys to tour and review; wherever they arrived, they inspected prisoners' fetters and shackles and provisions, and punished those who administered contrary to law.
translations.idiomatic: After cases were decided on review, the Ministry of Justice each first month sent inspectors to examine fetters, rations, and prison administration, punishing violations.

sentences.zh: 杻校鉗鎖皆有長短廣狹之制，量囚輕重用之。

translations.literal: Fetters, cangues, shackles, and locks all had regulations for length, shortness, breadth, and narrowness, applied according to the lightness or heaviness of the prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Fetters, cangues, shackles, and locks were prescribed in standard dimensions according to the severity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 囚二十日一訊，三訊而止，數不過二百。

translations.literal: Prisoners were interrogated once every twenty days; after three interrogations it stopped; the number did not exceed two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were interrogated every twenty days, no more than three sessions, and not more than two hundred blows.

sentences.zh: 凡杖，皆長三尺五寸，削去節目。

translations.literal: All beating sticks were three chi five cun long, with nodes and joints trimmed away.
translations.idiomatic: All beating sticks were three chi five cun long, with knots trimmed smooth.

sentences.zh: 訊杖，大頭徑三分二釐，小頭二分二釐。

translations.literal: Interrogation sticks: the large end had a diameter of three fen two li; the small end two fen two li.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation sticks measured three fen two li at the thick end and two fen two li at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 常行杖，大頭二分七釐，小頭一分七釐。

translations.literal: Regular execution sticks: the large end two fen seven li; the small end one fen seven li.
translations.idiomatic: Regular execution sticks measured two fen seven li at the thick end and one fen seven li at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 笞杖，大頭二分，小頭一分有半。

translations.literal: Chi sticks: the large end two fen; the small end one fen and a half.
translations.idiomatic: Chi sticks measured two fen at the thick end and one and a half fen at the thin end.

sentences.zh: 死罪校而加杻，官品勳階第七者，鎖禁之。

translations.literal: For capital crimes they wore the cangue and added fetters; for official rank and merit grades of the seventh degree, they were confined with locks.
translations.idiomatic: Capital offenders wore the cangue with fetters; officials of the seventh rank of merit were confined with locks.

sentences.zh: 輕罪及十歲以下至八十以上者、廢疾、侏儒、懷姙皆頌繫以待斷。

translations.literal: For light crimes and those from under ten years to over eighty, the disabled, dwarfs, and the pregnant—all were detained with loose bonds awaiting decision.
translations.idiomatic: Minor offenders, children under ten, the elderly over eighty, the disabled, dwarfs, and pregnant women were held with loose bonds pending judgment.

sentences.zh: 居作者著鉗若校，京師隸將作，女子隸少府縫作。

translations.literal: Those sentenced to penal labor wore shackles or the cangue; in the capital they were assigned to the Directorate of Works, and women to the Palace Domestic Service for needlework.
translations.idiomatic: Convicts doing penal labor wore shackles or the cangue; in the capital, men were assigned to the Directorate of Works and women to the Palace Domestic Service for sewing.

sentences.zh: 旬給假一日，臘、寒食二日，毋出役院。

translations.literal: Every ten days one day of leave was granted; on Laba and Cold Food Festival, two days—they were not to leave the labor compound.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten days they received one day off; on Laba and Cold Food Festival they received two days, but were not allowed to leave the labor compound.

sentences.zh: 病者釋鉗校、給假，疾差陪役。

translations.literal: The sick had shackles and the cangue removed and were granted leave; when the illness passed they joined labor duties.
translations.idiomatic: The sick had their shackles removed and were granted leave; once recovered, they resumed labor alongside the others.

sentences.zh: 謀反者男女奴婢沒為官奴婢，隸司農，七十者免之。

translations.literal: For plotting rebellion, male and female slaves were confiscated as government slaves and assigned to the Directorate of Agriculture; those seventy and older were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: In cases of treason, all male and female household slaves were confiscated as government slaves and assigned to the Directorate of Agriculture; those aged seventy or older were exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡役，男子入于蔬圃，女子入于廚饎。

translations.literal: For all labor service, men entered vegetable gardens, women entered kitchens for food preparation.
translations.idiomatic: In general labor service, men worked in vegetable gardens and women in kitchens.

sentences.zh: 流移人在道疾病，婦人免乳，祖父母、父母喪，男女奴婢死，皆給假，授程糧。

translations.literal: Exiles on the road who fell ill, women nursing infants, mourning for grandparents or parents, death of male or female slaves—all were granted leave and given journey rations.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles who fell ill en route, women nursing infants, those mourning grandparents or parents, and those whose male or female slaves had died were all granted leave and issued rations for the journey.

sentences.zh: 非反逆緣坐，六歲縱之，特流者三歲縱之，有官者得復仕。

translations.literal: Those implicated by kinship who were not in treason or rebellion cases were released after six years; special exiles after three years; those who held office could resume service.
translations.idiomatic: Kin implicated in crimes short of treason or rebellion were released after six years; those specially exiled after three; officials among them could return to office.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗以古者斷獄，訊於三槐、九棘，乃詔：「死罪，中書、門下五品以上及尚書等平議之；

translations.literal: At first, because Taizong considered that in antiquity in deciding cases one inquired at the Three Pagoda Trees and Nine Thorns, he decreed: "For capital crimes, fifth-rank officials and above of the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with the Ministry of State Affairs and others, would jointly deliberate."
translations.idiomatic: Early on, Taizong recalled that in antiquity judges held inquiries at the Three Pagoda Trees and Nine Thorns. He therefore decreed: "Capital cases are to be jointly reviewed by fifth-rank officials and above from the Secretariat and Chancellery, together with officials of the Ministry of State Affairs."

sentences.zh: 三品以上犯公罪流，私罪徒，皆不追身。

translations.literal: Third-rank officials and above who committed public offenses were sentenced to exile and those who committed private offenses to penal servitude, without requiring their physical apprehension.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of third rank and above who committed public offenses were sentenced to exile and those who committed private offenses to penal servitude, without requiring their physical apprehension.

sentences.zh: 」凡所以纖悉條目，必本於仁恕。

translations.literal: Every meticulous detailed provision was necessarily grounded in kindness and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Every fine-grained provision was rooted in kindness and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 然自張蘊古之死也，法官以失出為誡，有失入者，又不加罪，自是吏法稍密。

translations.literal: Yet from the death of Zhang Jungu onward, judicial officials took erroneous leniency as a warning; when there was erroneous severity, no penalty was imposed—from this the clerical law gradually tightened.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Jungu's death, however, judges treated lenient misjudgment as the cautionary lesson, while harsh misjudgment went unpunished—and from that point the law grew gradually stricter.

sentences.zh: 帝以問大理卿劉德威，對曰：「律，失入減三等，失出減五等。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Minister of Justice Liu Dewei, who replied: "According to the Code, erroneous severity reduces three degrees; erroneous leniency reduces five degrees."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned Minister of Justice Liu Dewei, who replied: "According to the Code, a judge who imposes too harsh a sentence is reduced three degrees in rank, but one who is too lenient is reduced five."

sentences.zh: 今失入無辜，而失出為大罪，故吏皆深文。

translations.literal: Now erroneous severity goes unpunished, yet erroneous leniency is treated as a great crime—therefore officials all apply harsh interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: "Today harsh misjudgment goes unpunished while lenient misjudgment is treated as a grave offense—so officials everywhere apply the harshest reading of the law."

sentences.zh: 」帝矍然，遂命失出入者皆如律，自此吏亦持平。

translations.literal: The emperor started in alarm and then ordered that both types of judicial error be handled according to the Code; from then on officials also held the middle way.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and ordered both kinds of judicial error punished according to the Code; from then on officials also held to the middle course.

sentences.zh: 十四年，詔流罪無遠近皆徙邊要州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, an edict ordered that all exile sentences, regardless of distance, were to be transferred to strategic border prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, an edict required all exiles, whatever the original distance, to be sent to key border prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後犯者寖少。

translations.literal: Thereafter offenders gradually became fewer.
translations.idiomatic: After that, repeat offenders dwindled.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又徙死罪以實西州，流者戍之，以罪輕重為更限。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, capital convicts were again transferred to populate Xizhou; exiles garrisoned it, with terms of service adjusted according to the severity of the crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, capital offenders were sent to populate Xizhou, with exiles assigned as garrison troops; terms of service varied with the gravity of the offense.

sentences.zh: 廣州都督瓽仁弘嘗率鄉兵二千助高祖起，封長沙郡公。

translations.literal: The Area Commander of Guangzhou, Tan Renhong, had once led two thousand local troops to help Gaozu rise, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Renhong, area commander of Guangzhou, had once raised two thousand local troops to aid Gaozu in his founding struggle and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 仁弘交通豪酋，納金寶，沒降獠為奴婢，又擅賦夷人。

translations.literal: Ren Hong colluded with powerful chieftains, accepted gold and treasures, seized surrendered Lao as slaves, and also levied taxes on his own authority from the barbarian peoples.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Hong colluded with tribal chieftains, accepted bribes of gold and jewels, enslaved surrendered Lao people, and unlawfully imposed levies on frontier tribes.

sentences.zh: 既還，有舟七十。

translations.literal: When he returned, he had seventy boats.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, he sailed home with seventy boatloads.

sentences.zh: 或告其贓，法當死。

translations.literal: Someone reported his corruption; by law he deserved death.
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported his graft, the law called for execution.

sentences.zh: 帝哀其老且有功，因貸為庶人，乃召五品以上，謂曰：「賞罰所以代天行法，今朕寬仁弘死，是自弄法以負天也。

translations.literal: The emperor, pitying his age and merit, commuted his sentence to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Rewards and punishments are how one executes the law on Heaven's behalf. Now in sparing Ren Hong from death I am manipulating the law and failing Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying his age and past service, commuted his sentence to commoner status. He then summoned officials of fifth rank and above and said: "Rewards and punishments are how the throne carries out Heaven's law. By sparing Ren Hong from death I am twisting the law and failing Heaven."

sentences.zh: 人臣有過，請罪於君，君有過，宜請罪於天。

translations.literal: When ministers err, they beg forgiveness from their lord; when the lord errs, he ought to beg forgiveness from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When a minister errs, he confesses to his sovereign; when the sovereign errs, he ought to confess to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其令有司設藳席于南郊三日，朕將請罪。

translations.literal: Let the officials set out a straw mat in the southern suburbs for three days—I shall beg forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: Have the officials lay out a straw mat in the southern suburbs for three days—I shall go there to confess.

sentences.zh: 」房玄齡等曰：「寬仁弘不以私而以功，何罪之請？

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling and others said: "In sparing Ren Hong you acted not from private favor but from his merit—what crime is there to confess?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling and others said: "You spared Ren Hong not from private favor but for his merit—what offense requires confession?"

sentences.zh: 」百僚頓首三請，乃止。

translations.literal: The hundred officials bowed their heads three times in entreaty, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: The assembled officials kowtowed three times in entreaty, and he relented.

sentences.zh: 太宗以英武定天下，然其天姿仁恕。

translations.literal: Taizong secured the realm through martial prowess, yet by nature he was kind and forgiving.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong had won the empire through martial brilliance, yet his nature was kind and forgiving.

sentences.zh: 初即位，有勸以威刑肅天下者，魏徵以為不可，因為上言王政本於仁恩，所以愛民厚俗之意，太宗欣然納之，遂以寬仁治天下，而於刑法尤慎。

translations.literal: When he first took the throne, some urged using stern punishments to awe the realm; Wei Zheng held this impossible and therefore addressed the throne on how kingship rests in kindness and grace, and the intent to cherish the people and enrich custom. Taizong gladly accepted this and hence governed the realm with leniency and kindness, and was especially cautious regarding penal law.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of his reign some advisers urged him to terrify the realm with harsh punishments. Wei Zheng argued against it, telling the emperor that humane government rests on kindness and grace—the spirit of cherishing the people and strengthening custom. Taizong gladly accepted this counsel and governed with leniency and mercy, exercising particular caution in applying criminal law.

sentences.zh: 四年，天下斷死罪二十九人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, executions throughout the realm totaled twenty-nine persons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, only twenty-nine death sentences were carried out empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 六年，親錄囚徒，閔死罪者三百九十人，縱之還家，期以明年秋即刑；

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he personally reviewed prisoners, commiserated with three hundred ninety condemned to death, released them to return home, setting the following autumn for execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he personally reviewed prisoners, took pity on three hundred ninety men sentenced to death, and sent them home with orders to return the following autumn for execution.

sentences.zh: 及期，囚皆詣朝堂，無後者，太宗嘉其誠信，悉原之。

translations.literal: When the deadline came, all the prisoners presented themselves at court with none tardy. Taizong praised their honesty and fully pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, every prisoner reported to court on time. Taizong admired their integrity and pardoned them all.

sentences.zh: 然嘗謂羣臣曰：「吾聞語曰『一歲再赦，好人喑啞』。

translations.literal: Yet he once told the assembled ministers: "I have heard the saying, 'Two amnesties in one year, and good people fall silent.'"
translations.idiomatic: Yet he once told his ministers: "I have heard the saying, 'Two amnesties in one year, and good people fall silent.'"

sentences.zh: 吾有天下未嘗數赦者，不欲誘民於幸免也。

translations.literal: Since I acquired the realm I have never issued amnesties frequently, because I do not wish to tempt the people toward hoping to escape punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Since I took the throne I have never issued frequent amnesties, because I do not wish to teach the people to count on escaping punishment."

sentences.zh: 」自房玄齡等更定律、令、格、式，訖太宗世，用之無所變改。

translations.literal: From the time Fang Xuanling and others revised the Code, Ordinances, Administrative Rules, and Formulas, through Taizong's reign they were used without alteration.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Fang Xuanling and others revised the Code, Ordinances, Administrative Rules, and Formulas, they remained unchanged through Taizong's reign.

sentences.zh: 高宗初即位，詔律學之士撰律疏。

translations.literal: When Gaozong first took the throne, he ordered scholars of penal law to compile a commentary on the Code.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Gaozong's reign, he ordered legal scholars to compile an annotated commentary on the Code.

sentences.zh: 又詔長孫无忌等增損格敕，其曹司常務曰留司格，頒之天下曰散頒格。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhangsun Wuji and others to revise administrative edicts; those for regular duties of the departments were called Retained Office Administrative Rules, and those promulgated empire-wide were called Broadly Issued Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhangsun Wuji and others to revise administrative edicts: rules for routine office business were called Retained Office Administrative Rules, and those issued empire-wide were called Broadly Issued Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 龍朔、儀鳳中，司刑太常伯李敬玄、左僕射劉仁軌相繼又加刊正。

translations.literal: During the Longshuo and Yifeng eras, Grand Master of Ceremonies for Punishments Li Jingxuan and Left Vice Director Liu Rengui successively made further revisions.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longshuo and Yifeng eras, Li Jingxuan, Grand Master of Ceremonies for Punishments, and Left Vice Director Liu Rengui successively made further revisions.

sentences.zh: 武后時，內史裴居道、鳳閣侍郎韋方質等又刪武德以後至于垂拱詔敕為新格，藏於有司，曰垂拱留司格。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, Inner Secretary Pei Judao, Vice Director of the Phoenix Pavilion Wei Fangzhi, and others again culled edicts and commands from Wude onward through the Chuigong era to form new Administrative Rules, stored among the relevant offices, called the Chuigong Retained Office Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Inner Secretary Pei Judao, Phoenix Pavilion Vice Director Wei Fangzhi, and others culled edicts from Wude through the Chuigong era into new Administrative Rules kept in the offices—the Chuigong Retained Office Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，中書令韋安石又續其後至於神龍，為散頒格。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Grand Counselor Wei Anshi continued it through the Shenlong era as Broadly Issued Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1, Grand Counselor Wei Anshi continued the compilation through the Shenlong era as Broadly Issued Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 睿宗即位，戶部尚書岑羲等又著太極格。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Minister of Revenue Cen Yi and others compiled the Taichi Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Minister of Revenue Cen Yi and others compiled the Taichi Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 玄宗開元三年，黃門監盧懷慎等又著開元格。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaiyuan under Xuanzong, Commissioner of the Yellow Gate Lu Huai-shen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 3, Yellow Gate Commissioner Lu Huai-shen and others compiled the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 至二十五年，中書令李林甫又著新格，凡所損益數千條，明年，吏部尚書宋璟又著後格，皆以開元名書。

translations.literal: By the twenty-fifth year, Grand Counselor Li Linfu compiled new Administrative Rules, adding and deleting several thousand articles in all; the next year, Minister of Civil Appointments Song Jing compiled later Administrative Rules—all titled with the Kaiyuan name.
translations.idiomatic: By Kaiyuan 25, Grand Counselor Li Linfu compiled new Administrative Rules, revising several thousand articles; the next year Minister of Civil Appointments Song Jing compiled a later set—both bearing the Kaiyuan title.

sentences.zh: 天寶四載，又詔刑部尚書蕭炅稍復增損之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianbao, an edict again ordered Minister of Justice Xiao Jiong to make further additions and deletions.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 4, an edict ordered Minister of Justice Xiao Jiong to revise the compilation once more.

sentences.zh: 肅宗、代宗無所改造。

translations.literal: Suzong and Daizong made no alterations.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong and Daizong made no alterations.

sentences.zh: 至德宗時，詔中書門下選律學之士，取至德以來制敕奏讞，掇其可為法者藏之，而不名書。

translations.literal: In Dezong's time, an edict ordered the Secretariat and Chancellery to select scholars of penal law, take edicts, memorials, and judicial reports from the Zhide era onward, extract what could serve as law and store it, without titling the compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Dezong, the Secretariat and Chancellery were ordered to select legal scholars, gather edicts, memorials, and judicial reports since the Zhide era, extract provisions fit to serve as law, and store them in an untitled compilation.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，刑部侍郎許孟容等刪天寶以後敕為開元格後敕。

translations.literal: In Xianzong's time, Vice Minister of Justice Xu Mengrong and others culled edicts after the Tianbao era into Later Edicts to the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xianzong, Vice Minister of Justice Xu Mengrong and others culled post-Tianbao edicts into the Later Edicts to the Kaiyuan Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 文宗命尚書省郎官各刪本司敕，而丞與侍郎覆視，中書門下參其可否而奏之，為大和格後敕。

translations.literal: Wenzong ordered the section directors of the Ministry of State Affairs each to cull their own department's edicts; then assistant directors and vice ministers reviewed them, and the Secretariat and Chancellery assessed their fitness and memorialized—forming the Later Edicts to the Dahe Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong ordered each section director in the Ministry of State Affairs to cull his department's edicts; assistant directors and vice ministers reviewed them, and the Secretariat and Chancellery judged their fitness before memorializing—the Later Edicts to the Dahe Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，刑部侍郎狄兼謩採開元二十六年以後至于開成制敕，刪其繁者，為開成詳定格。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaicheng, Vice Minister of Justice Di Jianmo collected edicts from the twenty-sixth year of Kaiyuan through Kaicheng, deleted the redundant portions, and formed the Kaicheng Detailed Administrative Rules.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3, Vice Minister of Justice Di Jianmo gathered edicts from Kaiyuan 26 through Kaicheng, trimmed the redundant portions, and produced the Kaicheng Detailed Administrative Rules.

sentences.zh: 宣宗時，左衞率府倉曹參軍張戣以刑律分類為門，而附以格敕，為大中刑律統類，詔刑部頒行之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong's time, Warehouse Clerk of the Left Guard Command Zhang Cui classified the penal code into categories, appended administrative edicts, and produced the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; an edict ordered the Ministry of Justice to promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, Left Guard Command warehouse clerk Zhang Cui arranged the penal code by category, appended administrative edicts, and compiled the Dazhong Unified Categories of Penal Law; the Ministry of Justice was ordered to promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 此其當世所施行而著見者，其餘有其書而不常行者，不足紀也。

translations.literal: These were what was enforced and visibly recorded in their time; as for the rest, works that existed but were not regularly applied are not worth recording.
translations.idiomatic: These were the compilations actually enforced and visibly in use in their day; the rest—texts that existed but were seldom applied—need not be recorded here.

sentences.zh: 書曰：「慎乃出令。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Be careful in issuing commands."
translations.idiomatic: The Documents say: "Be careful in issuing commands."

sentences.zh: 」蓋法令在簡，簡則明，行之在久，久則信，而中材之主，庸愚之吏，常莫克守之，而喜為變革。

translations.literal: For laws and commands lie in brevity—brief they are clear; in long application—long applied they are trusted. Yet middling rulers and mediocre officials commonly cannot uphold them and delight in making changes.
translations.idiomatic: Laws succeed when they are brief—brief laws are clear; they succeed when applied steadily—steady application wins trust. Yet middling rulers and mediocre officials often cannot maintain them and delight in change.

sentences.zh: 至其繁積，則雖有精明之士不能徧習，而吏得上下以為姦，此刑書之弊也。

translations.literal: When they accumulate in complexity, even keen-minded men cannot study them thoroughly, and clerks exploit gaps above and below to commit fraud—this is the defect of penal writings.
translations.idiomatic: Once they pile up in complexity, even sharp minds cannot master them, and clerks exploit the gaps to commit fraud—this is the curse of penal codes.

sentences.zh: 蓋自高宗以來，其大節鮮可紀，而格令之書，不勝其繁也。

translations.literal: Broadly speaking, from Gaozong onward there is little in the major outline worth recording, and the books of administrative rules and ordinances become unbearably numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly speaking, from Gaozong onward there is little worth recording in the broad outline, while the books of administrative rules and ordinances grow unbearably numerous.

sentences.zh: 高宗既昏懦，而繼以武氏之亂，毒流天下，幾至於亡。

translations.literal: Gaozong was both muddled and weak, and the Wu clan's turmoil followed; poison spread through the realm and the dynasty nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong was weak and indecisive, and the Wu clan's turmoil followed; cruelty spread through the realm and the dynasty nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 自永徽以後，武氏已得志，而刑濫矣。

translations.literal: From the Yonghui era onward, the Wu clan had already realized its ambitions, and punishments grew excessive.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yonghui era onward the Wu clan had already seized power, and punishments grew excessive.

sentences.zh: 當時大獄，以尚書刑部、御史臺、大理寺雜按，謂之「三司」，而法吏以慘酷為能，至不釋枷而笞棰以死者，皆不禁。

translations.literal: At the time major cases were jointly investigated by the Ministry of Justice within the Ministry of State Affairs, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review—called the "Three Offices." Legal clerks took brutal cruelty as merit; even those beaten to death without removing the cangue went unchecked.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases were jointly tried by the Ministry of Justice, the Censorate, and the Court of Judicial Review—a procedure called the "Three Offices." Magistrates competed in brutality; even beating prisoners to death without removing their cangues went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 律有杖百，凡五十九條，犯者或至死而杖未畢，乃詔除其四十九條，然無益也。

translations.literal: The Code provided for one hundred blows in fifty-nine articles all told; offenders sometimes died before the full count was delivered. An edict then abolished forty-nine of those articles, yet to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: The Code prescribed one hundred blows in fifty-nine articles; offenders sometimes died before the beating was finished. An edict then struck forty-nine of those articles, yet it did no good.

sentences.zh: 武后已稱制，懼天下不服，欲制以威，乃修後周告密之法，詔官司受訊，有言密事者，馳驛奏之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu had already assumed regency, feared the realm would not submit, and wished to control it through terror. She restored the Later Zhou system of informing on secrets, decreeing that when offices received interrogations and anyone spoke of confidential matters, they were to dispatch fast relay to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu had already assumed regency, feared the realm would not submit, and sought to rule through terror. She revived the Later Zhou system of secret denunciation, decreeing that when offices received interrogations and anyone reported confidential matters, they were to dispatch fast relay to the throne.

sentences.zh: 自徐敬業、越王貞、琅邪王沖等起兵討亂，武氏益恐。

translations.literal: After Xu Jingye, the Prince of Yue Zhen, the Prince of Langye Chong, and others raised armies to suppress the turmoil, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Jingye, Prince of Yue Zhen, Prince of Langye Chong, and others raised armies against her, the Wu clan grew even more fearful.

sentences.zh: 乃引酷吏周興、來俊臣輩典大獄，與侯思止、王弘義、郭弘霸、李敬仁、康暐、衞遂忠等集告事數百人，共為羅織，構陷無辜。

translations.literal: She then brought in cruel officials Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and their like to handle major cases, and together with Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others gathered several hundred informants to entrap and frame the innocent through fabricated charges.
translations.idiomatic: She then put cruel officials such as Zhou Xing and Lai Junchen in charge of major cases. With Hou Sizhi, Wang Hongyi, Guo Hongba, Li Jingren, Kang Wei, Wei Suizhong, and others, they assembled several hundred informants to weave false charges and frame the innocent.

sentences.zh: 自唐之宗室與朝廷之士，日被告捕，不可勝數，天下之人，為之仄足，如狄仁傑、魏元忠等皆幾不免。

translations.literal: From Tang imperial clansmen to court officials, daily denunciations and arrests were more than could be counted. People throughout the realm walked on tiptoe in fear; even men like Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong barely escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: From imperial clansmen to court officials, denunciations and arrests came daily beyond counting. People everywhere lived in dread; even men like Di Renjie and Wei Yuanzhong barely escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 左臺御史周矩上疏曰：「比姦憸告訐，習以為常。

translations.literal: Left Platform Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Recently treacherous accusations and denunciations have become habitual."
translations.idiomatic: Left Platform Censor Zhou Ju submitted a memorial saying: "Lately treacherous accusations and denunciations have become routine."

sentences.zh: 推劾之吏，以深刻為功，鑿空爭能，相矜以虐。

translations.literal: Interrogating officers take harsh severity as merit, contriving charges from nothing to compete in ability, each praising the other's cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogators treat harsh severity as merit, inventing charges from nothing to outdo one another, each boasting of the other's cruelty.

sentences.zh: 泥耳囊頭，摺脅籤爪，縣髮燻耳，臥鄰穢溺，刻害支體，糜爛獄中，號曰『獄持』；

translations.literal: Packing the ears and bagging the head, folding the armpits and pricking the fingernails, suspending the hair and smoking the ears, making prisoners lie beside filth and urine, carving and maiming the limbs until they putrefy in prison—they call this 'prison holding.'
translations.idiomatic: They pack the ears and bag the head, fold the armpits and prick the fingernails, suspend the hair and smoke the ears, force prisoners to lie beside filth and urine, and mutilate the limbs until flesh rots in the cell—they call this "prison holding."

sentences.zh: 閉絕食飲，晝夜使不得眠，號曰『宿囚』。

translations.literal: Cutting off food and drink, keeping prisoners from sleep day and night—they call this 'overnight detention.'
translations.idiomatic: They cut off food and drink and keep prisoners from sleep day and night—they call this "overnight detention."

sentences.zh: 殘賊威暴，取快目前。

translations.literal: They mutilate, savage, and terrorize for immediate gratification.
translations.idiomatic: They mutilate, brutalize, and terrorize for immediate gratification.

sentences.zh: 被誣者苟求得死，何所不至？

translations.literal: Those falsely accused, if only to obtain death—what would they not do?
translations.idiomatic: Those falsely accused, if only to obtain death—what would they not confess?

sentences.zh: 為國者以仁為宗，以刑為助，周用仁而昌，秦用刑而亡。

translations.literal: Those who govern a state take benevolence as their foundation and punishment as their aid. Zhou employed benevolence and flourished; Qin employed punishment and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Those who govern a state take benevolence as their foundation and punishment as their support. Zhou relied on benevolence and flourished; Qin relied on punishment and perished.

sentences.zh: 願陛下緩刑用仁，天下幸甚！

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will relax punishments and employ benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will ease punishments and govern with benevolence—the realm would be greatly blessed!

sentences.zh: 」武后不納。

translations.literal: Empress Wu did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 麟臺正字陳子昂亦上書切諫，不省。

translations.literal: Palace Library Corrector Chen Zi'ang also submitted a forceful remonstrance, which went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Library corrector Chen Zi'ang also submitted a forceful remonstrance, which went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 及周興、來俊臣等誅死，后亦老，其意少衰，而狄仁傑、姚崇、宋璟、王及善相與論垂拱以來酷濫之冤，太后感寤，由是不復殺戮。

translations.literal: After Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were executed, the Empress had also grown old and her intent somewhat waned. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together discussed the cruel excesses and injustices since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved to understanding, and from then on she no longer carried out slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhou Xing, Lai Junchen, and others were executed, the Empress had also grown old and her zeal somewhat faded. Di Renjie, Yao Chong, Song Jing, and Wang Jishan together discussed the cruel excesses and wrongful convictions since the Chuigong era; the Empress Dowager was moved, and from then on she no longer carried out mass killings.

sentences.zh: 然其毒虐所被，自古未之有也。

translations.literal: Yet the poison and cruelty that had spread were unmatched since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the poison and cruelty that had spread were unmatched since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 大足元年，乃詔法司及推事使敢多作辯狀而加語者，以故入論。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazu, an edict declared that legal offices and special investigatory commissioners who dared to compose lengthy written defenses and add fabricated language would be prosecuted for deliberate misjudgment.
translations.idiomatic: In Dazu 1, an edict declared that legal offices and special investigatory commissioners who dared to compose lengthy written defenses and add fabricated language would be prosecuted for deliberate misjudgment.

sentences.zh: 中宗、韋后繼以亂敗。

translations.literal: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed with disorder and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong and Empress Wei followed with disorder and ruin.

sentences.zh: 玄宗自初即位，勵精政事，常自選太守、縣令，告戒以言，而良吏布州縣，民獲安樂；

translations.literal: From the time Xuanzong first took the throne, he applied himself diligently to governance, often personally selecting prefects and magistrates and admonishing them in person; good officials spread through the prefectures and counties, and the people enjoyed peace.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Xuanzong first took the throne, he applied himself diligently to governance, often personally selecting prefects and magistrates and admonishing them in person; capable officials spread through the prefectures and counties, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 二十年間，號稱治平，衣食富足，人罕犯法。

translations.literal: For twenty years the age was called well governed; food and clothing were ample and few people broke the law.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty years the age was called well governed; food and clothing were ample and few people broke the law.

sentences.zh: 是歲刑部所斷天下死罪五十八人，往時大理獄，相傳鳥雀不栖，至是有鵲巢其庭樹，羣臣稱賀，以為幾致刑錯。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Justice throughout the realm executed fifty-eight capital sentences. It was formerly said of the Court of Judicial Review prison that not even birds would roost there; now magpies nested in its courtyard trees. The assembled ministers offered congratulations, thinking punishment had nearly fallen into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Justice executed fifty-eight capital sentences empire-wide. It was once said of the Court of Judicial Review prison that not even birds would roost there; now magpies nested in its courtyard trees. The assembled ministers offered congratulations, believing punishments had nearly fallen into disuse.

sentences.zh: 然而李林甫用事矣，自來俊臣誅後，至此始復起大獄，以誣陷所殺數十百人，如韋堅、李邕等皆一時名臣，天下冤之。

translations.literal: Yet Li Linfu was already in power. From Lai Junchen's execution until now, major cases were raised again for the first time; dozens and hundreds were killed through framed charges. Men like Wei Jian and Li Yong were leading ministers of the age, and the realm deemed it unjust.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Li Linfu was already in power. Since Lai Junchen's execution, major cases were raised again for the first time; dozens and hundreds were killed through framed charges. Men like Wei Jian and Li Yong were leading ministers of their day, and the realm deemed it unjust.

sentences.zh: 而天子亦自喜邊功，遣將分出以擊蠻夷，兵數大敗，士卒死傷以萬計，國用耗乏，而轉漕輸送，遠近煩費，民力既弊，盜賊起而獄訟繁矣。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Son of Heaven also delighted in frontier glory, dispatching generals in separate columns to strike the barbarians; armies suffered great defeats, with soldiers dead and wounded numbering in the tens of thousands. State revenues were drained; transport and grain shipment burdened near and far. Once the people's strength was exhausted, bandits rose and lawsuits proliferated.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the emperor also delighted in frontier glory, dispatching generals in separate columns to strike the barbarians; armies suffered great defeats, with tens of thousands of soldiers dead or wounded. State revenues were drained, and grain transport burdened the realm. Once the people's strength was exhausted, bandits rose and lawsuits proliferated.

sentences.zh: 天子方惻然，詔曰：「徒非重刑，而役者寒暑不釋械繫。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was deeply moved and decreed: "Penal servitude is not a heavy punishment, yet those serving labor are not released from shackles in heat or cold."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and decreed: "Penal servitude is not a heavy punishment, yet labor convicts are not released from shackles in heat or cold."

sentences.zh: 杖，古以代肉刑也，或犯非巨蠧而棰以至死，其皆免，以配諸軍自效。

translations.literal: The staff, in antiquity a substitute for corporal mutilation—yet some whose offenses were not grave enormities were beaten to death. All such cases are pardoned; let them be assigned to armies to redeem themselves through service."
translations.idiomatic: The staff, in antiquity a substitute for corporal mutilation—yet some whose offenses were not grave were beaten to death. All such cases are pardoned; let them be assigned to armies to redeem themselves through service."

sentences.zh: 民年八十以上及重疾有罪，皆勿坐。

translations.literal: Commoners eighty years and older, and those gravely ill who have committed offenses, are all not to be prosecuted."
translations.idiomatic: Commoners eighty years and older, and those gravely ill who have committed offenses, are not to be prosecuted."

sentences.zh: 侍丁犯法，原之俾終養。

translations.literal: When supporting sons violate the law, pardon them so they may complete their filial duty of care."
translations.idiomatic: When sons supporting elderly parents violate the law, pardon them so they may complete their filial duty."

sentences.zh: 」以此施德其民。

translations.literal: In this way he dispensed kindness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: In this way he dispensed kindness to the people.

sentences.zh: 然巨盜起，天下被其毒，民莫蒙其賜也。

translations.literal: Yet great bandits arose; the realm suffered their poison, and the people never tasted his grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet great bandits arose; the realm suffered their ravages, and the people never tasted his grace.

sentences.zh: 安、史之亂，偽官陸大鈞等背賊來歸，及慶緒奔河北，脅從者相率待罪闕下，自大臣陳希烈等合數百人。

translations.literal: In the An-Shi rebellion, puppet officials such as Lu Dajun and others deserted the rebels to submit; when Qingxu fled to Hebei, coerced followers successively came to the palace gate to await judgment—from Grand Counselor Chen Xilie and others, several hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: During the An-Shi rebellion, puppet officials such as Lu Dajun and others deserted the rebels to submit; when Qingxu fled to Hebei, coerced followers came in succession to the palace gate to await judgment—from Grand Counselor Chen Xilie and others, several hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫李峴、中丞崔器等為三司使，而肅宗方喜刑名，器亦刻深，乃以河南尹達奚珣等三十九人為重罪，斬于獨柳樹者十一人，珣及韋恆腰斬，陳希烈等賜自盡於獄中者七人，其餘決重杖死者二十一人。

translations.literal: Li Xian, Censor-in-Chief, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi and others were made Three Offices commissioners. Suzong was then enamored of harsh law, and Qi was also severe. Thirty-nine men including Henan Intendant Daxi Xun were judged for grave offenses: eleven beheaded at the Lone Willow Tree; Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist; seven including Chen Xilie were granted permission to kill themselves in prison; the remaining twenty-one were sentenced to heavy beating until death.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Xian and Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi and others were appointed Three Offices commissioners. Suzong was then enamored of harsh law, and Qi was also severe. Thirty-nine men including Henan Intendant Daxi Xun were judged for grave offenses: eleven beheaded at the Lone Willow Tree; Xun and Wei Heng were cut in two at the waist; seven including Chen Xilie were granted permission to kill themselves in prison; the remaining twenty-one were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 以歲除日行刑，集百官臨視，家屬流竄。

translations.literal: Executions were carried out on New Year's Eve; all officials were assembled to witness; families were exiled and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were carried out on New Year's Eve with all officials assembled to witness; families were exiled and banished.

sentences.zh: 初，史思明、高秀巖等皆自拔歸命，聞珣等被誅，懼不自安，乃復叛。

translations.literal: At first Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had all willingly defected and submitted. Hearing that Xun and others had been executed, they feared for their safety and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shi Siming, Gao Xiuyan, and others had all willingly defected and submitted. Hearing that Xun and others had been executed, they feared for their lives and rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 而三司用刑連年，流貶相繼。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Three Offices applied punishments year after year, and exile and demotion followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Three Offices applied punishments year after year, and exile and demotion followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 及王璵為相，請詔三司推覈未已者，一切免之。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu became chancellor, he requested an edict that all cases still under Three Offices investigation be entirely pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yu became chancellor, he requested an edict pardoning all cases still under Three Offices investigation.

sentences.zh: 然河北叛人畏誅不降，兵連不解，朝廷屢起大獄。

translations.literal: Yet rebels in Hebei, fearing execution, refused to surrender; warfare continued without end, and the court repeatedly launched major investigations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet rebels in Hebei, fearing execution, refused to surrender; warfare continued without end, and the court repeatedly launched major investigations.

sentences.zh: 肅宗後亦悔，歎曰：「朕為三司所悞。

translations.literal: Suzong later also regretted it and sighed: "I was misled by the Three Offices."
translations.idiomatic: Suzong later regretted it and sighed: "I was misled by the Three Offices."

sentences.zh: 」臨崩，詔天下流人皆釋之。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he decreed that all exiles throughout the realm be released.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he decreed that all exiles throughout the realm be released.

sentences.zh: 代宗性仁恕，常以至德以來用刑為戒。

translations.literal: Daizong was by nature kind and forgiving, and constantly took the use of punishments since the Zhide era as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Daizong was by nature kind and forgiving, and constantly took the harsh punishments since the Zhide era as a warning.

sentences.zh: 及河、洛平，下詔河北、河南吏民任偽官者，一切不問。

translations.literal: When the Yellow and Luo regions were pacified, he issued an edict that officials and commoners in Hebei and Henan who had served puppet offices would not be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow and Luo regions were pacified, he issued an edict that officials and commoners in Hebei and Henan who had served puppet offices would not be questioned at all.

sentences.zh: 得史朝義將士妻子四百餘人，皆赦之。

translations.literal: Captured were more than four hundred wives and children of Shi Chaoyi's soldiers and officers—all were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred wives and children of Shi Chaoyi's soldiers and officers were captured—all were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩反，免其家，不緣坐。

translations.literal: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, his family was exempted and not implicated by kinship.
translations.idiomatic: When Pugu Huai'en rebelled, his family was exempted and not punished by kinship implication.

sentences.zh: 劇賊高玉聚徒南山，啗人數千，後擒獲，會赦，代宗將貸其死，公卿議請為葅醢，帝不從，卒杖殺之。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and devoured several thousand people. Later he was captured; an amnesty was issued. Daizong was about to spare his life. The chief ministers discussed asking that he be minced and salted; the emperor did not agree, and in the end he was beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: The notorious bandit Gao Yu gathered followers on South Mountain and killed several thousand people. After he was captured, an amnesty was proclaimed. Daizong was inclined to spare his life, but the chief ministers argued he should be dismembered and salted. The emperor did not consent, yet in the end Gao Yu was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 諫者常諷帝政寬，故朝廷不肅。

translations.literal: Remonstrators often satirized the emperor's lenient governance, and so the court lacked discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators often criticized the emperor's lenient rule, saying the court had grown undisciplined.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「艱難時無以逮下，顧刑法峻急，有威無恩，朕不忍也。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said: "In times of hardship one could not reach down to the people; one looked only to harsh and urgent penal law—authority without kindness. I cannot bear that.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "In hard times one could not reach down to the people; all one could do was rely on harsh penal law—stern authority without kindness. I cannot bear that.

sentences.zh: 」即位五年，府縣寺獄無重囚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of his accession, prefectural, county, and tribunal prisons held no serious prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Five years into his reign, prefectural, county, and tribunal prisons held no serious prisoners.

sentences.zh: 故時，別敕決人捶無數。

translations.literal: In former times, special edicts sentencing people to beating were without number.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, special edicts ordering beatings had been without number.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔曰：「凡制敕與一頓杖者，其數止四十；

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict stated: "For all imperial orders granting one session of beating, the number shall stop at forty;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoying, an edict stated: "For all imperial orders imposing one session of beating, the number shall not exceed forty;

sentences.zh: 至到與一頓及重杖一頓、痛杖一頓者，皆止六十。

translations.literal: For those granted one session of beating, one session of heavy beating, or one session of painful beating, all shall stop at sixty.
translations.idiomatic: For cases involving one full session of beating, one session of heavy beating, or one session of painful beating, the limit shall be sixty strokes.

sentences.zh: 德宗性猜忌少恩，然用刑無大濫。

translations.literal: Dezong was by nature suspicious and lacking in kindness, yet in applying punishments there was no great abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong was suspicious by nature and sparing of kindness, yet punishments under him were not greatly abused.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎班宏言：「謀反、大逆及叛、惡逆四者，十惡之大也，犯者宜如律。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Ban Hong said: "Rebellion, great treason, desertion, and wicked treason—these four are among the greatest of the Ten Abominations; offenders should be treated according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Ban Hong said, "Rebellion, great treason, desertion, and wicked treason—these four are among the gravest of the Ten Abominations, and offenders should be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 其餘當斬、絞刑者，決重杖一頓處死，以代極法。

translations.literal: All others liable to decapitation or strangulation shall undergo one session of heavy beating and then be put to death, in place of the supreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: All others liable to decapitation or strangulation shall instead receive one session of heavy beating followed by death, as a substitute for the supreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 」故時，死罪皆先決杖，其數或百或六十，於是悉罷之。

translations.literal: Formerly, all capital crimes were first subjected to beating, the number sometimes one hundred or sixty; now all this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly all capital sentences had been preceded by beating, sometimes as many as a hundred or sixty strokes; now this practice was entirely abolished.

sentences.zh: 憲宗英果明斷，自即位數誅方鎮，欲治僭叛，一以法度，然於用刑喜寬仁。

translations.literal: Xianzong was heroic, resolute, and clear in judgment. From his accession he repeatedly executed regional commanders, wishing to govern usurpation and rebellion, applying the law uniformly; yet in using punishments he favored leniency and benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong was heroic, resolute, and clear in judgment. From his accession he repeatedly punished regional commanders, seeking to suppress usurpation and rebellion through uniform application of the law; yet in punishing crimes he favored leniency and benevolence.

sentences.zh: 是時，李吉甫、李絳為相。

translations.literal: At this time Li Jifu and Li Jiang served as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Li Jifu and Li Jiang served as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 吉甫言：「治天下必任賞罰，陛下頻降赦令，蠲逋負，賑飢民，恩德至矣。
