translations.literal: Jifu said: "To govern the realm one must rely on rewards and punishments. Your Majesty has frequently issued amnesties, remitted overdue levies, and relieved the hungry—Your grace has reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu said, "To govern the realm one must rely on rewards and punishments. Your Majesty has frequently issued amnesties, remitted overdue taxes, and relieved the hungry—Your kindness could scarcely be greater.

sentences.zh: 然典刑未舉，中外有懈怠心。

translations.literal: Yet canonical punishments have not been enforced, and within and without the court there is slackness of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the canonical punishments have not been enforced, and throughout the court and bureaucracy minds have grown slack.

sentences.zh: 」絳曰：「今天下雖未大治，亦未甚亂，乃古平國用中典之時。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Today the realm, though not greatly well governed, is also not greatly chaotic—it is a time like ancient tranquil states when the moderate code was applied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang said, "The realm today, though not greatly well governed, is also not greatly chaotic—it is a time like those of old when tranquil states applied the moderate code.

sentences.zh: 自古欲治之君，必先德化，至暴亂之世，始專任刑法。

translations.literal: Since antiquity rulers who wished to govern began with moral transformation; only in ages of violent chaos did they rely exclusively on penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity rulers who wished to govern well began with moral transformation; only in ages of violent chaos did they rely exclusively on penal law.

sentences.zh: 吉甫之言過矣。

translations.literal: Jifu's words go too far.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu has gone too far.

sentences.zh: 」憲宗以為然。

translations.literal: Xianzong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 司空于頔亦諷帝用刑以收威柄，帝謂宰相曰：「頔懷姦謀，欲朕失人心也。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yu Di also remonstrated that the emperor should use punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors: "Di harbors treacherous designs and wishes me to lose the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yu Di also urged the emperor to use harsh punishments to recover sovereign authority. The emperor told the chancellors, "Di harbors treacherous designs and wants me to lose the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」元和八年，詔：「兩京、關內、河東、河北、淮南、山南東西道死罪十惡、殺人、鑄錢、造印，若彊盜持仗劫京兆界中及它盜贓踰三匹者，論如故。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, an edict stated: "For the Two Capitals, Guannei, Hedong, Hebei, Huainan, and the eastern and western circuits of Shannan, death penalties for the Ten Abominations, murder, counterfeiting coin, forging seals, armed robbers raiding within the Jingzhao boundaries, and other theft of goods exceeding three bolts of silk—the original penalties shall apply.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Yuanhe, an edict stated: "In the Two Capitals, Guannei, Hedong, Hebei, Huainan, and the eastern and western circuits of Shannan, death penalties for the Ten Abominations, murder, counterfeiting coin, forging seals, armed robbery within the Jingzhao boundaries, and theft of goods exceeding three bolts of silk shall be judged as before.

sentences.zh: 其餘死罪皆流天德五城，父祖子孫欲隨者，勿禁。

translations.literal: All other death crimes shall be exiled to the Five Cities of Tiande; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wish to accompany them shall not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: All other capital crimes shall be commuted to exile in the Five Cities of Tiande; fathers, grandfathers, sons, and grandsons who wish to accompany the offender shall not be forbidden.

sentences.zh: 」蓋刑者，政之輔也。

translations.literal: For punishments are the auxiliary of governance.
translations.idiomatic: For punishments are the auxiliary of governance.

sentences.zh: 政得其道，仁義興行，而禮讓成俗，然猶不敢廢刑，所以為民防也，寬之而已。

translations.literal: When governance obtains the Way, benevolence and righteousness rise and flourish, and courtesy and yielding become custom; yet one still dare not abolish punishments—they serve as safeguards for the people, and one need only moderate them.
translations.idiomatic: When governance follows the Way, benevolence and righteousness flourish and courtesy and yielding become custom; yet one still dare not abolish punishments—they serve as safeguards for the people, and need only be moderated.

sentences.zh: 今不隆其本、顧風俗謂何而廢常刑，是弛民之禁，啟其姦，由積水而決其防。

translations.literal: Now, without elevating the root yet abandoning ordinary punishments—what of customs and mores?—this is to loosen the people's restraints, open the way to villainy, like breaking a dike when water has already accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: Now, without strengthening the foundation yet abandoning ordinary punishments—what becomes of customs and mores?—this loosens the people's restraints and opens the way to villainy, like breaking a dike when water has already accumulated.

sentences.zh: 故自玄宗廢徒杖刑，至是又廢死刑，民未知德，而徒以為幸也。

translations.literal: Thus from Xuanzong's abolition of penal servitude and beating, down to this further abolition of death penalties, the people had not yet learned virtue and regarded it merely as good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Thus from Xuanzong's abolition of penal servitude and beating down to this further abolition of the death penalty, the people had not yet learned virtue and regarded the change merely as good fortune.

sentences.zh: 穆宗童昏，然頗知慎刑法，每有司斷大獄，令中書舍人一人參酌而輕重之，號「參酌院」。

translations.literal: Muzong was childish and dull-witted, yet he was fairly mindful in applying penal law. Whenever the responsible offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to review and adjust severity, called the "Review and Deliberation Office."
translations.idiomatic: Muzong was immature and dull-witted, yet he was fairly conscientious about penal law. Whenever responsible offices tried major cases, he ordered one Secretariat drafter to review and adjust the severity of sentences—an office called the "Review and Deliberation Office."

sentences.zh: 大理少卿崔𣏌奏曰：「國家法度，高祖、太宗定制二百餘年矣。

translations.literal: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Yuan memorialized: "The state's laws and institutions were established by Gaozu and Taizong more than two hundred years ago.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Cui Yuan memorialized: "The state's laws and institutions were established by Gaozu and Taizong more than two hundred years ago.

sentences.zh: 周禮正月布刑，張之門閭及都鄙邦國，所以屢丁寧，使四方謹行之。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou state that in the first month punishments are promulgated and posted at gates and lanes, in districts and prefectures, and in the states—all to repeat admonitions and make the four quarters carefully observe them.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribe that in the first month punishments are promulgated and posted at gates and lanes, in districts and prefectures, and throughout the realm—all to repeat admonitions and ensure the four quarters carefully observe them.

sentences.zh: 大理寺，陛下守法之司也。

translations.literal: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Judicial Review is Your Majesty's office for upholding the law.

sentences.zh: 今別設參酌之官，有司定罪，乃議其出入，是與奪繫於人情，而法官不得守其職。

translations.literal: Now a separate Review and Deliberation office has been established; after the responsible offices fix guilt, it deliberates increase or decrease—life and death depend on personal sentiment, and judicial officers cannot perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Now a separate office of review and deliberation has been established: after the responsible offices determine guilt, it revises the sentence up or down—so that life and death depend on personal sentiment and judicial officers cannot perform their duties.

sentences.zh: 昔子路問政，孔子曰：『必也正名乎。

translations.literal: Formerly Zilu asked about governance, and Confucius said: 'What is necessary is to rectify names.'
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Zilu asked about governance, and Confucius said, 'What is necessary is to rectify names.'

sentences.zh: 』臣以為參酌之名不正，宜廢。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that the name 'Review and Deliberation' is not correct and should be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that the name 'Review and Deliberation' is improper and should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」乃罷之。

translations.literal: The office was then abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The office was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 大和六年，興平縣民上官興以醉殺人而逃，聞械其父，乃自歸。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Dahe, Shangguan Xing, a commoner of Xingping County, killed a man while drunk and fled; hearing that his father had been put in fetters, he surrendered himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Dahe, Shangguan Xing, a commoner of Xingping County, killed a man while drunk and fled; when he learned his father had been put in fetters, he surrendered himself.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹杜悰、御史中丞宇文鼎以其就刑免父，請減死。

translations.literal: Jingzhao Intendant Du Cong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding, because he submitted to punishment to save his father, requested commutation of the death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Intendant Du Cong and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding, because Xing had surrendered to save his father, requested that his death sentence be reduced.

sentences.zh: 詔兩省議，以為殺人者死，百王所守；

translations.literal: An edict ordered deliberation by the Two Departments, which held that murderers die—this all kings have upheld;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Two Departments to deliberate; they held that murderers must die—a principle upheld by kings through the ages;

sentences.zh: 若許以生，是誘之殺人也。

translations.literal: If life were granted, this would be to entice men to murder.
translations.idiomatic: To grant him life would be to entice men to murder.

sentences.zh: 諫官亦以為言。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials also spoke to this effect.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating officials said the same.

sentences.zh: 文宗以興免父囚，近於義，杖流靈州，君子以為失刑。

translations.literal: Wenzong, because Xing freed his imprisoned father, which was close to righteousness, sentenced him to beating and exile to Lingzhou; men of principle considered this a failure of penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong, considering that Xing had freed his imprisoned father—a deed close to righteousness—sentenced him to beating and exile to Lingzhou; men of principle regarded this as a failure of justice.

sentences.zh: 文宗好治，躬自謹畏，然閹宦肆孽不能制。

translations.literal: Wenzong loved good governance and personally exercised caution and restraint, yet eunuchs ran wild in wickedness and he could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong loved good governance and personally exercised caution and restraint, yet eunuchs ran wild and he could not control them.

sentences.zh: 至誅殺大臣，夷滅其族，濫及者不可勝數，心知其冤，為之飲恨流涕，而莫能救止。

translations.literal: Eventually ministers were executed and their clans exterminated; those wrongfully implicated were beyond counting. He knew in his heart they were unjustly condemned, wept tears of bitter grief for them, yet could not save or stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually ministers were executed and their clans exterminated; those wrongfully implicated were beyond counting. Wenzong knew in his heart they were unjustly condemned and wept bitter tears for them, yet could not save or stop it.

sentences.zh: 蓋仁者制亂，而弱者縱之，然則剛彊非不仁，而柔弱者仁之賊也。

translations.literal: For the benevolent restrain disorder, while the weak indulge it; thus firmness and strength are not un-benevolent, while weakness and softness are the enemies of benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: The benevolent restrain disorder; the weak indulge it. Firmness and strength are not unkind, but weakness and softness are the enemies of kindness.

sentences.zh: 武宗用李德裕誅劉稹等，大刑舉矣，而性嚴刻。

translations.literal: Wuzong, using Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; great punishments were carried out, and his nature was stern and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong, relying on Li Deyu, executed Liu Zhen and others; harsh punishments were fully applied, and his nature was stern and harsh.

sentences.zh: 故時，竊盜無死，所以原民情迫於飢寒也，至是贓滿千錢者死，至宣宗乃罷之。

translations.literal: Formerly petty theft incurred no death penalty—this was to forgive the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of goods worth a thousand cash incurred death; this was not abolished until Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly petty theft did not incur the death penalty, forgiving the people's plight under hunger and cold; now theft of goods worth a thousand cash brought death—a policy not abolished until Xuanzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 而宣宗亦自喜刑名，常曰：「犯我法，雖子弟不宥也。

translations.literal: Xuanzong also delighted in penal law and often said: "Whoever violates my law, even if kin, shall not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong also delighted in penal law and often said, "Whoever violates my law shall not be pardoned, even if he is my own kin.

sentences.zh: 」然少仁恩，唐德自是衰矣。

translations.literal: Yet he lacked benevolence and grace; from this Tang virtue declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked benevolence and grace, and from this Tang virtue declined.

sentences.zh: 蓋自高祖、太宗除隋虐亂，治以寬平，民樂其安，重於犯法，致治之美，幾乎三代之盛時。

translations.literal: From Gaozu and Taizong's removal of Sui cruelty and disorder, governing with leniency and moderation, the people rejoiced in their security and feared to break the law—the beauty of good governance nearly matched the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozu and Taizong's removal of Sui cruelty and disorder, their lenient and moderate governance made the people secure and wary of breaking the law—their achievement in good governance nearly matched the flourishing age of the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 考其推心惻物，其可謂仁矣！

translations.literal: Considering their putting heart into things and compassion for others, they may be called benevolent!
translations.idiomatic: Considering their wholehearted devotion and compassion for all beneath Heaven, they may truly be called benevolent!

sentences.zh: 自高宗、武后以來，毒流邦家，唐祚絕而復續。

translations.literal: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the realm; Tang's mandate was severed and then renewed.
translations.idiomatic: From Gaozong and Empress Wu onward, poison flowed through the realm; the Tang mandate was severed and then renewed.

sentences.zh: 玄宗初勵精為政，二十年間，刑獄減省，歲斷死罪纔五十八人。

translations.literal: At first Xuanzong exerted himself in governance; within twenty years criminal cases were reduced, and death sentences adjudicated yearly amounted to only fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xuanzong exerted himself in governance; within twenty years criminal cases were reduced, and yearly death sentences amounted to only fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 以此見致治雖難，勉之則易，未有為而不至者。

translations.literal: From this one sees that achieving good governance, though difficult, becomes easy with effort—nothing attempted fails to succeed.
translations.idiomatic: From this one sees that achieving good governance, though difficult, becomes easy with effort—nothing attempted with diligence fails to succeed.

sentences.zh: 自此以後，兵革遂興，國家多故，而人主規規，無復太宗之志。

translations.literal: From this time onward warfare arose, the state faced many troubles, and sovereigns were petty-minded, no longer possessing Taizong's aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: From this time onward warfare arose and the state faced many troubles; sovereigns grew petty-minded and no longer possessed Taizong's aspiration.

sentences.zh: 其雖有心於治者，亦不能講考大法，而性有寬猛，凡所更革，一切臨時苟且，或重或輕，徒為繁文，不足以示後世。

translations.literal: Even those with some mind for governance could not examine and apply the great law; their natures had leniency and severity; all reforms were mere temporary expedients, sometimes heavy, sometimes light—empty formalities insufficient to instruct posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Even those with some desire to govern well could not examine and apply the great law; with natures ranging from lenient to severe, all their reforms were temporary expedients—sometimes harsh, sometimes lenient—empty formalities that could not instruct posterity.

sentences.zh: 而高祖、太宗之法，僅守而存。

translations.literal: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were barely preserved and kept in existence.
translations.idiomatic: The laws of Gaozu and Taizong were barely preserved.

sentences.zh: 故自肅宗以來，所可書者幾希矣；

translations.literal: Thus from Suzong onward, what could be recorded was almost nothing;
translations.idiomatic: Thus from Suzong onward, almost nothing worth recording remained;

sentences.zh: 懿宗以後，無所稱焉。

translations.literal: After Yizong, there was nothing to praise.
translations.idiomatic: After Yizong, there was nothing worth praising.
